selection_reasoning: I selected 'mine birch_fence_gate' as the single atomic task. This task is straightforward and observable: the agent must locate a birch fence gate in the scene and mine (break) it. It requires no deep Minecraft domain knowledge — just finding the block and breaking it. The task is easily verifiable by checking whether the birch_fence_gate block has been removed from its position and/or whether the agent has picked up the item. Since we are selecting exactly 1 task, the dependency graph is a single node with no edges.

milestones.description: Uses inventory_has because when a birch fence gate is mined (broken), it drops itself as an item that ends up in the player's inventory. The player starts with no birch_fence_gate items, so having at least 1 confirms the block was successfully mined and collected.

scene_description: A flat grass platform with a small birch fence enclosure placed ~3-5 blocks from spawn. The enclosure has a birch fence gate on one side (facing east). The player is given a wooden axe to mine the gate efficiently. The scene is compact and the fence structure is easily visible from spawn after a brief look-around.
task_text: Find the birch fence gate in the nearby fence structure and mine (break) it to collect it.
design_notes: The fence enclosure is a 3x3 ring of birch fences with one side replaced by a birch_fence_gate (at ~3,0,~4, facing east). The player spawns at ~0,0,~0 and needs to walk ~5 blocks diagonally to reach the structure. A wooden axe is provided to speed up mining. The flat grass platform and cleared air ensure good visibility. The gate is at ground level (y+0 relative to player feet) so it's easy to target and break.
